items.content_html:
Follow-up to commit f20cd90 (where log() was defined for missing argument errors).

Options like --file and --attr properly check if an argument was provided:

--file|-f)
    if [ -z "$1" ]; then
        log "$0: '$i' requires an argument"
        exit 1
    fi

However, other flags consuming arguments (--root, --channel, --system, --flake, --max-jobs) unconditionally ran shift 1. When invoked with a trailing flag without an argument (e.g. nixos-install --root), shift 1 fails on an empty parameter list, causing bash to silently abort with exit code 1 under set -e.

Changes:

  • Add [ -z "$1" ] checks before shifting for --max-jobs, --root, --system, --flake, and --channel.
  • Report $0: '$i' requires an argument via log and exit with 1.

Testing:

$ nix-build -A nixos-install
/nix/store/znqsv634klrargdgha5nz6j390cxmjv2-nixos-install

$ ./result/bin/nixos-install --root
./result/bin/nixos-install: '--root' requires an argument
$ echo $?
1

$ ./result/bin/nixos-install --channel
./result/bin/nixos-install: '--channel' requires an argument
$ echo $?
1

$ ./result/bin/nixos-install --max-jobs
./result/bin/nixos-install: '--max-jobs' requires an argument
$ echo $?
1

items.content_html:
When nixos-enter is invoked with an option requiring an argument (--root, --system, or --command/-c) as the final parameter, the script unconditionally executes shift 1 on an empty parameter list:

$ sudo nixos-enter --root
$ echo $?
1

Because shift 1 fails on the empty positional parameters and set -e is active, the script silently aborts with exit code 1 without providing any diagnostic message to the user.

Changes:

  • Add a check [ -z "$1" ] before shifting for --root, --system, and --command/-c
  • Output $0: '$i' requires an argument to stderr and exit with 1

Testing:

Verified manually with ./result/bin/nixos-enter:

$ ./result/bin/nixos-enter --root
./result/bin/nixos-enter: '--root' requires an argument
$ echo $?
1

$ ./result/bin/nixos-enter -c
./result/bin/nixos-enter: '-c' requires an argument
$ echo $?
1

items.content_html:
TL;DR: The PR forces deterministic ordering between rw-etc and /rw-etc

Context

My / is on tmpfs. Historically, I've kept the entire /etc folder on persistent storage via a bind mount to a persisted location (/etc -> /persist/etc). This doesn't work with system.etc.overlay since it requires it's own mount on /etc to work, locking you out completely from your machine, almost identically to #319524

Fix

The fix, I've found, is to persist .rw-etc instead which seems to be where mutable files go. However, I can see that ATM the rw-etc unit relies on / only for ordering. This won't work properly if you have /.rw-etc as a separate mount which is required for those follow an root level 'impermanence' setup like myself since there's technically nothing stopping rw-etc running before the /.rw-etc mount gets created first. Thus, I've added it to the RequiresMountsFor

items.content_html:
Another attempt at a module for https://github.com/vouch/vouch-proxy. Should address #299381 (comment).

The module is intended to run one instance of vouch-proxy per domain/app to be protected (that is, per entry in services.vouch-proxy.clients), as oauth2 clients should not be shared between applications. By default, it configures every nginx virtualHost matched by a services.vouch-proxy.clients.<name>.domain to use vouch-proxy.

Minimal working example below, where everything runs on the same host.
services.nginx.virtualHosts.myAppDomain1 and services.nginx.virtualHosts.myAppDomain2 are assumed to be already defined (as they would be without vouch-proxy), and the clients myoauthclient1 and myoauthclient2 should be configured for vouch-proxy in the oauth2 provider.
This example uses kanidm, which the module takes care of (for every client) on vouch-proxy's side if kanidmUrl is set.
For other oauth2 providers, the correct auth_url, token_url and user_info_url need to be set either globally, under services.vouch-proxy.settings.oauth, or, if required (as it is with kanidm for user_info_url), per client under services.vouch-proxy.clients.<name>.settings.oauth.

  services.vouch-proxy = {
    enable = true;
    kanidmUrl = config.services.kanidm.server.settings.domain;
  };

  services.vouch-proxy.clients = {
    myoauthclient1 = {
      port = 12345;
      domain = "myAppDomain1";
      environmentFile = "./myApp1.env"; # this file should contain `VOUCH_JWT_SECRET` and `OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET`
    };
    myoauthclient2 = {
      port = 23456;
      domain = "myAppDomain2";
      environmentFile = "./myApp2.env";
    };
  };

items.content_html:
Adds a NixOS module for T3 Code:

services.t3code = {
  enable = true;
  user = "alice";
};

Upstream ships t3 service install, which turns on linger, installs a pinned t3 from npm into ~/.t3/runtime, and runs it under a launcher that updates itself. Not quite what we want from a Nix-installation. This module runs t3 serve straight from the store as a system unit with User=, using the same kill and OOM settings as upstream's unit. Remote self-update requests are disabled, because the server isn't running under upstream's launcher.

  • user is required. Agents act with that user's repositories and provider credentials, so a dedicated system user makes no sense. State lives in the user's ~/.t3, which the t3 CLI uses too.
  • host defaults to 127.0.0.1 (same as upstream) and port to 3773. openFirewall is available for remote access.
  • Telemetry (PostHog) is off by default through T3CODE_TELEMETRY_ENABLED = mkDefault "false".
  • t3 serve creates a one-time admin pairing token on every start and prints it, with a QR code, to stdout. LogFilterPatterns keeps it out of the journal. Users pair with t3 auth pairing create instead. The token expires after 5 minutes, and upstream has no way to turn it off yet.
  • Provider CLIs come from the existing package overrides, e.g. package = pkgs.t3code.override { enableClaude = true; }.

The VM test waits for the "server is ready" log line, not only for the port to open. Upstream accepts TCP connections before its HTTP handler is attached, and requests sent in that window are never answered: pingdotgg/t3code#12215.

cc @iamanaws @qweered as t3code maintainers: this adds passthru.tests.nixos to the package. Happy to add you as module co-maintainers if you want to be.

AI disclosure: the module, test were drafted with Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5) and reviewed by me, this description being proof-read too. The commits carry Assisted-by: trailers. The upstream behavior relied on here (unit template, default bind address, telemetry switch, startup pairing token, self-update gating, startup race) was checked against the shipped 0.0.40 bundle and reproduced locally and in the VM test.

Add the somewm wayland compositor, an AwesomeWM port to wayland, along with a programs.somewm NixOS module.
Homepage: https://somewm.org/
Source: https://github.com/trip-zip/somewm

The package wraps somewm with -s to import WAYLAND_DISPLAY and XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP into the systemd and D-Bus environments. xdg-desktop-portal-wlr needs both for screencast.

The trailing cat > /dev/null drains the pipe somewm opens for the startup command. Without it, apps launched from somewm inherit a closed stdout, and Electron apps crash with EPIPE.

Note: somewm 2.1.0 is out, but it builds its own patched wlroots 0.20.2 (subprojects/wlroots.wrap carries a rounded-corners diff). That doesn't fit linking the system wlroots_0_20, so this PR stays on 2.0.1.

items.content_html:
Adds a NixOS module for configuring PCI device passthrough using VFIO.

The new virtualisation.vfio module:

  • Loads the required VFIO kernel modules;
  • Binds configured PCI vendor/device IDs to vfio-pci;
  • Optionally includes VFIO modules in the initrd;
  • Configures soft dependencies so specified host drivers load after vfio-pci;

The module is crafted based on the linked Arch wiki page.

The NixOS VM test uses QEMU’s pci-testdev with an emulated IOMMU to verify the correct loading of the kernel modules and the binding of the device to vfio-pci.

I also tested the module on my own system and I am currently using it for passthrough of my laptop's discrete GPU to a QEMU VM.

AI usage

I wrote the full module and test by hand. I asked an LLM to review the changes, which resulted in minor changes (mostly spelling).

Adds a module that can ergonomically put multiple separate clients behind multiple OAuth2 Proxy, as compared to the existing module under services.oauth2-proxy, which only supports a single oauth2-client.

Automatically configures standard host routes for the host services.oauth2-proxy-multi.clients.<name>.domain for caddy or nginx if either of them is enabled (depending on config.services.caddy.enable or config.services.nginx.enable). These can be disabled via services.oauth2-proxy-multi.configureCaddy = false or services.oauth2-proxy-multi.configureNginx = false.

Minimal working example below, where everything runs on the same host.
The clients myoauthclient1 and myoauthclient2 should both be configured for use with oauth2-proxy in the oauth2 provider.
This example uses kanidm, which the module takes care of (for every client) on oauth2-proxy's side if services.oauth2-proxy-multi.kanidmDomain is set.
For other oauth2 providers, the correct oidc_issuer_url needs to be set either globally under services.oauth2-proxy-multi.settings.oidc_issuer_url, or per client under services.oauth2-proxy-multi.clients.<name>.settings.oidc_issuer_url.

services.oauth2-proxy-multi = {
  enable = true;
  kanidmDomain = config.services.kanidm.server.settings.domain;
};

services.oauth2-proxy-multi.clients = {
  myoauthclient1 = {
    domain = "myAppDomain1";
    settings = {
      upstreams = "http://[::1]:12345";
      client_secret_file = "./myApp1ClientSecret.txt";
      cookie_secret_file = "./myApp1CookieSecret.txt";
    };
  };
  myoauthclient2 = {
    domain = "myAppDomain2";
    settings = {
      upstreams = "http://[::1]:23456";
      client_secret_file = "./myApp2ClientSecret.txt";
      cookie_secret_file = "./myApp2CookieSecret.txt";
    };
  };
};

items.content_html:
The generated interface name is currently always the network attribute name, which must be prefixed by the radio name. Sharing one interface name (e.g. mld0) among link BSSs of a Wi-Fi 7 multi-link device on different radios, with mld_ap=1, is required for MLO support. An MLO AP therefore cannot be configured without rewriting the generated config from dynamicConfigScripts.

Add networks.<name>.interfaceName, defaulting to the attribute name, and emit it as the interface=/bss= value. Attribute names still order the primary BSS first and name the ACL files. The primary BSS must keep the radio's name, since systemd device dependencies reference it.

Things done

Tested on NixOS running on a GL.inet GL-BE9300, all 3 MLO links were created (2g/5g/6g) under a single SSID.

items.content_html:
The pixelfed module puts pkgs.ffmpeg on the path of the pixelfed units. Pixelfed uses ffmpeg and ffprobe only to process the media that users upload. This change uses pkgs.ffmpeg-headless in place of pkgs.ffmpeg.

ffmpeg-headless has the same codecs as ffmpeg. ffmpeg also has ffplay, SDL, PulseAudio and VDPAU, which a server does not use. Through SDL, they also add PipeWire and avahi to the system closure, while avahi 0.8 is subject to CVE-2025-59529, while a candidate fix has yet to land at time of filing. The mastodon and peertube modules use ffmpeg-headless for this same reason.

The closure of the server node of nixosTests.pixelfed.standard:

size avahi, PipeWire, SDL
before 2227 MiB yes
after 1621 MiB no

items.content_html:
Add services.keyd.applicationMapper, which when enabled creates the keyd group, adds the configured users to it, and starts the keyd-application-mapper user service

The keyd daemon setgids into the keyd group on startup, without CAP_SETGID the service crashes whenever that group exists

Usage example:

services.keyd = {
  enable = true;
  applicationMapper = {
    enable = true;
    users = [ "alice" ];
  };
  keyboards = { ... };
};

Fixes #290161

Assisted by Qwen3.8-27B

This PR introduces an variety of changes to the smartd module:

  • Shellcheck validation of the notification script
  • Dynamic detection of the X11 session to send notifications to.
  • Systemd unit hardening
  • NixOS tests for all notification mechanisms + various device detection
  • Remove dbus package as an optional dep, replace with busctl from systemd

The changes should be backwards compatible with the exception of sendmail implementations that requires further relaxed hardening (if there are any).
